title: Frontline ask mapping with continuous probability scoring and quick-econ snapshot
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: Sales and CS send a high volume of enterprise feature asks that vary in product fit, engineering effort, and commercial upside. We need a repeatable front-line artifact that: 1) quickly turns signals into a concise problem statement canvas; 2) assigns a continuous probability score (0-100%) representing likelihood of acceptance/ROI; and 3) produces a 1-slide quick-econ snapshot to accelerate go/no-go decisions.

Scope: Build a Playcard and light-weight process for Sales/CS to submit requests and for PMs to perform a 10-20 minute triage. Deliverables: triage Playcard template, scoring rubric, Slack intake shortcut, a Notion intake form, and a brief training doc for AE/CS leads. Not building end-to-end automation in this ticket — focus on workflow, scoring, and handoff criteria.
solution_options: Option A - Playcard + Manual Scoring: Create a one-page Playcard template that Sales/CS complete. PM performs a 15-min review and assigns continuous probability (0-100) and rough effort band. Quick-econ uses ARR uplift heuristics.
Option B - Intake Form + Heuristics: Structured Notion/form captures p0 fields. Basic heuristic auto-suggests probability band based on account tier and use-case; PM confirms or adjusts.

Option C - Pilot Automation: Wire form to a light automation that scores requests and surfaces top candidates in a weekly 'frontline triage' digest for PMs and Eng leads. Requires small infra work (depends on ENG-1842).
acceptance_criteria: A Playcard template exists in Notion and is published to Sales/CS with one example filled out
A scoring rubric (0-100) with clear signal mapping (account ARR, strategic alignment, integration complexity, regulatory needs) is documented
A short Quick-Econ snapshot template (1 slide) is created with formulas to estimate ARR uplift, cost, and payback time
Slack intake shortcut and Notion intake form are live and have been used by at least two AE/CS teams in pilot
PM-led triage runbook produced (10-20 minute steps) and one pilot triage completed with annotated decision rationale
